Hi Sarah — looping in details from the marketplace side.

Thanks for the PO draft and the ramp schedule. Here’s how we typically handle this on AWS Marketplace for a private offer with a region-entity split and staged capacity:

1) Signatory/entity split: AWS supports updating the buyer entity for a private offer but it’s treated as an amendment to the existing private offer. We’ll submit an amendment request that lists both entities and the region mapping. AWS requires both (a) the exact legal name and tax ID you want on invoices and (b) a signed amendment document from the buyer entity. Once AWS processes the amendment, the private offer is updated and invoices can be generated per the mapped entity. Typical turn time from submission is 3–5 business days unless AWS requests additional evidence.

2) Phased activation / staged commitments: We can encode a staged activation schedule in the private offer by creating acceptance gates tied to the dates in your ramp schedule. Operationally we do this by publishing an acceptance checklist (SOW-style) for each phase. The private offer will mark the later phases as pending until the respective checklist is accepted (manual signature or DocuSign). Billing for committed units begins when that phase is accepted.

Required items from your side:
- Exact legal entity name(s) and tax IDs for each entity to appear on the private-offer amendment.
- Signed PO or acceptance for initial phase to trigger the first activation.
- Point of contact for signing (name, title, email, phone).

I’ll prepare a short amendment template and an acceptance checklist for phase-1 that you can circulate to your legal/procurement.

Proposed timeline:
- Tue (6/29): We share amendment template + DocuSign flow
- Wed–Thu (6/30–7/1): TideWave legal signs amendment and we submit to AWS
- 3–5 business days for AWS processing (if no follow-ups)

If your procurement prefers staggered invoicing (EU invoices to GmbH, US to Labs), Jonas can confirm the invoice setup and any ledger/tax notes.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Marketplace Programs, Redwood Inference

Hi all — quick confirmation from finance.

Short answer on invoicing: for AWS private offers the marketplace typically issues the invoice to the buyer entity listed in the private-offer amendment. That means we should be able to get separate invoice documents for EU-region usage (to TideWave Analytics GmbH) and US-region usage (to TideWave Labs, Inc.) provided the amendment clearly maps SKUs/usage regions to each entity. Redwood will not need to re-issue invoices for those marketplace-billed items.

Operational notes:
- We’ll submit the amendment with the two entities and region mapping. If AWS accepts it as-is, invoices flow to the respective entities. If AWS requires a consolidated buyer, we’ll request a marketplace workaround but that may introduce a short delay and require additional paperwork.
